items.title: William "Ba Ba" Ridgley Interview, 1959-06-02
items.q: William Ridley, trombone. Emma Barrett, piano.

ctx.x: No. People sang, but they were good. Old time hymn made them up their self and so on like that. And I was a Sunday school boy. I attended the Ross Chapel M.E. Center School in Jefferson College. Now I've been working in the church for about 28 years. And I didn't think anything else could stop me. But we want to name the Tuxedo band that Mr. Sim Black named. That was Chinese, no, Henry Zeno on drum. Tom Benton, banjo. Sam Dutre, clarinet. Celestine, cornet. George Foster, bass. William Ridley, trombone. Emma…

Can you tell me about the first records you made when you made those phonograph records? Who was in the band? There were some that they were made for okay. A Careless Love and the Black and White, let's see, was it the Black Rag or Black and White Rag?

items.title: William "Ba Ba" Ridgley Interview, 1961-04-07
items.q: And they used to come around us when we played and they liked the way that Sweet Emma used to juggle that piano and different things like that.

ctx.x: Yeah. I got a phone up I've been trying to get all yesterday.

She don't want to answer you. She wants that phone out of me. Tell me she's doing good. She's getting by one of the old tuxedo band people that had noticed and wanted a short bang, you know. And they didn't like her. Now who did give us our start with her was Miss Caroline Benjamin. St. John and Joseph Street. Now she was a good banjo, a guitar player and a good piano, a good musician. And her and several other young white girls. And they used to come around us when we played and they liked the way that Sweet…
Did they sit in with her, you know, and with you all and play some of those society people? Would they ever play with you? Who was that?

items.title: William "Ba Ba" Ridgley Interview, 1961-04-11
items.q: Emma is sitting at the piano.

ctx.x: Oh, yes. And it's got you and then it's got Schatz. Willie Joseph, that's Kaiser. Emma is sitting at the piano. Arthur Durbany. And a saxophone player from St. Louis. It looks like he's playing a tenor or a C melody. I can't tell for sure. Must be a tenor. And then Robert Hall is another saxophone player. Willie Bontong playing the banjo and somebody...
That must have been the one I was trying to tell you about there, you see, that saxophone player that I had when they went out. What's his name?
